name: usb-history
desc: Free, open-source USB device history viewer for Windows — see every stick, phone and drive ever connected. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Full connection history** — every USB device ever plugged in, with first and last seen timestamps
✅ **Rich identity data** — vendor, product, VID/PID, serial and device class columns sortable and searchable
✅ **Mount point mapping** — shows which drive letter a storage device took during use
✅ **Connected-now view** — a live tab of currently attached devices with safe eject shortcuts
✅ **Export for audits** — CSV with all fields for compliance checks and asset tracking
✅ **No kernel driver** — reads standard device registry data; safe on locked-down workstations
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | First-seen and last-seen dates | **Yes** | Yes | Connect only | No |
| Mount point history | **Yes** | Partial | No | Current only |
| CSV audit export | **Yes** | Yes | No | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Zip | Zip | With OS |
faqQ: how to see USB devices connected to my computer history?
faqA: Windows forgets devices the moment they are unplugged unless you dig through registry keys nobody documents. usb-history reads that log and shows every device with identity data and first and last seen dates, exportable for audits. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline, no admin driver required.
s1: Dark table (#121418, cyan #22D3EE): rows per device with vendor, VID/PID and Last seen columns, search field typed SanDisk, export button.
s2: Device drawer: serial number, device class, mount history E then F, connected-now badge, safe eject action link.
s3: Audit view: date range filter, CSV export preview with 87 rows, duplicate serial warning chip in amber.
